questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents for laser hair removal of her legs. The dermatologist selects a wavelength of 800 nm with a pulse duration of 30 milliseconds. Which principle explains why this specific pulse duration was chosen for targeting the hair follicle?
opts: The pulse duration must exceed the thermal relaxation time to allow heat dissipation
The pulse duration must be shorter than or equal to the thermal relaxation time to confine heat within the target
Longer pulse durations increase the depth of penetration regardless of wavelength
The pulse duration should match the optical window of 600-1200 nm
questions.exp: According to the theory of selective photothermolysis, the pulse duration must be shorter than or equal to the target's thermal relaxation time (TRT) to confine heat within the target and prevent thermal damage to surrounding tissue. Hair follicles have a TRT of 40-100 milliseconds, so a 30 ms pulse appropriately confines the thermal energy.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman undergoes a deep chemical peel. Within seconds of the procedure causing dermal injury, vasoconstriction occurs at the wound site. Which mediators are primarily responsible for this immediate vascular response?
questions.exp: Immediate vasoconstriction following endothelial disruption is elicited by the local release of serotonin and thromboxane A2 (TXA2). This response minimizes hemorrhage at the injury site during the haemostasis phase.

questions.q: A 45-year-old solid organ transplant recipient presents with a 0.8 cm nodular lesion on the nasal ala. Biopsy reveals basal cell carcinoma with morpheaform histology. Which feature MOST strongly indicates Mohs micrographic surgery as the treatment of choice?
questions.exp: Location in the H-zone (mask areas of the face including nose) is the highest priority indication for Mohs surgery. Although the morpheaform subtype, immunosuppression, and potential for iceberg phenomenon also support MMS, anatomical location in the H-zone takes precedence in appropriate use criteria.

questions.q: A plastic surgeon is planning scar revision for a long linear burn contracture across the neck. Why would multiple small continuous Z-plasties be preferred over a single large Z-plasty in this scenario?
opts: Single large Z-plasty provides insufficient tissue lengthening
Multiple Z-plasties allow better blood supply to flaps and superior scar camouflage
Single large Z-plasty cannot achieve 90° directional change
Multiple Z-plasties require smaller lateral limb angles for the same effect
questions.exp: For long linear contractures, multiple small continuous Z-plasties are preferred because they distribute transverse tension across smaller flaps, ensuring safer blood supply and vastly superior scar camouflage compared to a single massive Z-plasty which would create overly large flaps.

questions.q: A dermatologist performing a glycolic acid peel observes faint erythema on the patient's face. What is the most appropriate next step in the procedure?
opts: Apply another layer to achieve deeper penetration
Neutralize with water or sodium bicarbonate solution
Allow the peel to remain for additional 10 minutes
questions.exp: Glycolic acid (an AHA) is time-dependent and requires manual neutralization as it cannot coagulate skin proteins. Faint erythema represents the clinical endpoint, and the acid must be neutralized with water or a weak buffer like sodium bicarbonate to prevent continued penetration, over-peeling, and potential scarring.

questions.q: A dermatologist is using octyl cyanoacrylate (Dermabond) for wound closure. Which of the following statements regarding tissue adhesives is TRUE?
opts: They are ideal for closing wounds under significant tension
Subcutaneous implantation is safe due to biocompatible degradation products
They exhibit bacteriostatic properties against Staphylococci and Pseudomonas
Their binding strength is equivalent to a 3-0 suture
questions.exp: Tissue adhesives like octyl cyanoacrylate act as an antimicrobial barrier with bacteriostatic properties against organisms like Staphylococci, Pseudomonas, and E. coli. They are contraindicated for wounds under tension and must NEVER be used subcutaneously as they cause severe tissue necrosis due to toxic byproducts.

questions.q: A 32-year-old patient presents with periorbital puffiness and dark circles but has minimal skin wrinkling. Which lower lid blepharoplasty approach is most appropriate, and why?
opts: Transcutaneous approach because it provides better access to orbital fat
Transconjunctival approach because it avoids external scarring and has lower ectropion risk
Transcutaneous approach because it allows simultaneous orbicularis muscle excision
Transconjunctival approach because it is preferred in patients with significant skin laxity
questions.exp: Transconjunctival blepharoplasty is ideal for younger patients with baggy eyes and puffiness but minimal skin laxity. This approach leaves no visible external scar and carries a significantly lower risk of ectropion by avoiding dissection through the anterior eyelid planes.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man develops a tense, painful hemorrhagic bulla on his lower leg 24 hours after cryotherapy for an actinic keratosis. What is the most appropriate management of this blister?
opts: Complete debridement of the blister roof and application of silver sulfadiazine
Aspiration with an 18-gauge needle inserted laterally while leaving the roof intact
Oral antibiotics and observation without intervention
Unroofing the blister and applying a hydrocolloid dressing
questions.exp: For tense and highly painful blisters following cryotherapy, aseptic drainage using an 18-gauge needle inserted laterally is recommended. The blister roof must be left entirely intact to serve as a natural, sterile biologic dressing that promotes healing.

questions.q: A keloid scar following earlobe piercing is treated with surgical excision. Which adjuvant therapy should be initiated within 24-48 hours post-operatively to reduce recurrence?
opts: Superficial radiotherapy or intralesional corticosteroid injection
questions.exp: Early adjuvant therapy within 24-48 hours after keloid excision is critical for preventing recurrence. Superficial radiotherapy or intralesional triamcinolone injection are the most effective adjuvants. Without adjuvant therapy, keloid recurrence rates exceed 50-80%.

questions.q: A Q-switched laser with nanosecond pulse duration is most appropriate for targeting which of the following structures based on their thermal relaxation time?
questions.exp: Melanosomes have a diameter of 0.5-1.0 μm and a thermal relaxation time of less than 1 microsecond (250-1000 nanoseconds). This extremely short TRT necessitates nanosecond (Q-switched) or picosecond laser pulses to confine heat within these small targets according to selective photothermolysis principles.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman undergoes excision of a melanocytic nevus on her back. The surgeon plans to use buried dermal sutures that will provide prolonged tensile strength support for at least 4-6 weeks in this high-tension area. Which suture material would be most appropriate?
questions.exp: Polydioxanone (PDS II) retains approximately 70-74% of tensile strength at 2 weeks and 50% at 4 weeks, making it ideal for high-tension areas requiring prolonged support. Monocryl loses tensile strength rapidly (0% at 21 days), while catgut and Vicryl Rapide have even shorter strength retention periods.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman with Fitzpatrick skin type V undergoes cryotherapy for a seborrheic keratosis on her forearm. Which cell type is most susceptible to damage at the lowest freezing temperature, making her at highest risk for a specific long-term complication?
questions.exp: Melanocytes are exquisitely cryosensitive and undergo cell death at temperatures of -4°C to -7°C, well before keratinocytes are destroyed. This makes hypopigmentation the most significant long-term complication in dark-skinned individuals and may be permanent if freeze duration exceeds 30 seconds.

questions.exp: Japanese physician credited with an early follicular punch hair transplantation technique (1930s). Restored hair in scarred/burned scalp decades before Orentreich

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman is undergoing upper eyelid blepharoplasty. During surgical planning, the surgeon performs the pinch test. What is the primary purpose of this maneuver?
opts: To assess the function of the levator palpebrae superioris muscle
To determine the exact amount of redundant skin to be excised
To evaluate the position of the preaponeurotic fat pad
To measure the distance from the lid margin to the orbital rim
questions.exp: The pinch test is performed to determine the precise amount of excess skin to excise during upper blepharoplasty. The surgeon grasps increasing amounts of skin until the upper eyelid margin begins to slightly evert, indicating the maximum safe excision.

questions.q: A 52-year-old woman presents with longitudinal melanonychia of the thumbnail. Dermoscopy shows irregular brown lines with variable spacing and thickness. What is the most appropriate biopsy technique?
opts: Punch biopsy of the nail plate
Nail plate avulsion with punch biopsy of nail bed
Lateral longitudinal excisional biopsy including nail matrix
Shave biopsy of the proximal nail fold
questions.exp: Lateral longitudinal excisional biopsy is the gold standard for melanonychia suspicious for subungual melanoma as it samples the entire length of the pigmented band including the nail matrix origin. This allows complete histopathological assessment of Breslow depth while minimizing nail dystrophy.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman with oily skin and comedonal acne undergoes a chemical peel. During the procedure, the dermatologist observes a white crystalline precipitate forming on the skin surface without requiring any neutralizing agent. Which property of the peeling agent explains this phenomenon?
opts: Small molecular size enabling deep dermal penetration
questions.exp: The white crystalline precipitate (pseudofrost) is characteristic of salicylic acid (BHA) peels. The lipophilic nature of salicylic acid allows it to penetrate sebaceous follicles, and as the hydroethanolic vehicle evaporates, the acid precipitates on the skin, making the peel self-limiting and self-neutralizing.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with a post-burn contracture band across the antecubital fossa limiting elbow extension. The surgeon plans a Z-plasty with limbs angled at 60° from the central limb placed along the scar. What percentage of tissue lengthening and change in scar direction will be achieved with this design?
questions.exp: The classic 60° Z-plasty is the gold standard technique that achieves 75% gain in tissue length along the original scar axis and causes a precise 90° change in the direction of the central limb. This allows optimal redirection of scars perpendicular to relaxed skin tension lines.

questions.q: Identify the clinical sign / pathological finding shown:
questions.exp: Violaceous (lilac) periorbital erythema with eyelid edema. Pathognomonic cutaneous sign of dermatomyositis

questions.q: During wound healing, the stabilized fibrin clot serves multiple functions beyond haemostasis. Which of the following is NOT a recognized function of the fibrin clot in wound healing?
opts: Acts as a provisional wound matrix providing structural scaffold
Serves as a reservoir of growth factors including PDGF and TGF-β
Provides adhesion substrates for migrating epithelial cells
Directly stimulates collagen synthesis by myofibroblasts
questions.exp: The fibrin clot functions as a provisional wound matrix, a reservoir of growth factors (PDGF, TGF-β, EGF, VEGF), and provides adhesion substrates (fibrin, fibronectin, vitronectin) for cell migration. Direct stimulation of collagen synthesis by myofibroblasts is not listed as a clot function.

questions.q: Identify the surgical instrument shown in the image:
questions.exp: A kind of small spring forceps, used for removing unwanted hair. In electroepilation to pull out destroyed hair

questions.q: A 62-year-old man undergoes Mohs micrographic surgery for dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP) on the trunk. Which immunohistochemical marker is most useful to augment margin assessment during this procedure?
questions.exp: CD34 immunohistochemistry is used to augment Mohs surgery for DFSP, helping to identify tumor cells extending in unpredictable honeycomb or finger-like projections beyond clinical margins. This dramatically reduces recurrence rates compared to standard wide excision.

questions.q: Which characteristic distinguishes monofilament sutures from braided/multifilament sutures?
opts: Higher capillarity leading to increased infection risk
Greater pliability and superior handling characteristics
Low coefficient of friction with reduced tissue drag
Better knot security due to lower memory
questions.exp: Monofilament sutures have a low coefficient of friction, allowing smooth passage through tissue with minimal drag, and low capillarity that reduces infection risk. In contrast, braided sutures have increased capillarity (harboring bacteria) but offer better handling and knot security due to their greater pliability and lower memory.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman undergoes excision of a large lipoma on her back. Post-operatively, she develops a fluctuant swelling at the surgical site with serous fluid aspirated on needle aspiration. Which of the following is the most appropriate primary preventive measure during surgery to avoid this complication?
opts: Application of topical cyanoacrylate adhesive on skin surface
Placement of deep buried sutures to eliminate dead space
Use of non-absorbable sutures for epidermal closure
Tight tying of superficial skin sutures
questions.exp: The complication described is a seroma, which develops due to dead space accumulation. Dead space is eliminated by executing a precise layered closure that firmly approximates each tissue plane using deep buried sutures, preventing fluid accumulation that acts as a nidus for infection.
